scope: Quick literature search and inspection of primary theorem statements; not an independent proof audit or fresh Lean build of the external repository.
target: Deterministic worst-case total bit complexity 2^(C*ell/sqrt(log(ell+2)))*(ell+1)^d for every semiprime, from binary input, with fixed C and d.
finding: No stronger deterministic all-input factoring bound was identified in this search. This is a bounded search result, not an exhaustive priority claim.

results.title: A log-log speedup for exponent one-fifth deterministic integer factorisation
Subexponential Deterministic Factoring
results.bound: One finite-alphabet Mathlib TM2 machine computes Nat.minFac from binary input; for every integer k>=1 there exists C_k such that time on every ell-bit input is at most C_k*2^floor(ell/k).
results.guarantee: The authors report a completed Lean proof. This review inspected the public statement and top-level proof declaration but did not replay the build or audit its full proof closure.
results.comparison: The qualitative 2^o(ell) statement does not imply the project's explicit rate. Their SqrtLogLogConjecture states that sharper rate as an unproved proposition.
results.possibleUse: Inspect the verified compilation and machine-cost components for reuse with attribution. Their counting engine is described as a re-proved variant of the Anthropic construction, rather than an imported OpenAI theorem. No reuse or integration has been performed.

results.authors: H. W. Lenstra Jr. and Carl Pomerance
results.title: A rigorous time bound for factoring integers
results.comparison: Faster asymptotic rate, but not the deterministic worst-case guarantee sought here.
